title: Ordered 64-byte matrix copy
summary: Recovered VA 0x426fd0 (50 bytes) as a genuine thiscall member returning this. Copies four 16-byte snapshots in ascending order, preserving unaligned and overlap behavior. Callers use stack matrices and object fields at +0x41c/+0x45c. No helpers or global side effects.
test_description: 16992 original-versus-C++ cases across 16 source alignments, 177 destination offsets, and six MXCSR settings. Includes exact alias, both overlap directions, offsets around 16-byte boundaries, adjacent and disjoint storage. Checks returned destination, every byte of 256-byte arenas including untouched guards/source, ordered-block model, and unchanged MXCSR.
known_limits: Matrix element meaning, row/column convention and original C++ method name are unresolved.

Valid readable/writable 64-byte regions are required; invalid pointers, page faults, volatile memory and concurrent modification are outside this recovery's contract. Original block accesses are single MOVDQU operations; portable byte loops do not reproduce fault granularity or concurrent access behavior.
Behavioral recovery only; no matching-byte claim or whole-game recovery claim.
